text.en: Find the notes of line 1: each one waits until you're on it.
The same songbook also prints a related spiritual, "Did You Hear How Dey Crucified My Lord?", and notes that "Were You There When They Crucified My Lord" seemed "to be universally more popular".

source.en: R. Nathaniel Dett, ed., Religious Folk-Songs of the Negro as Sung at Hampton Institute (1927), p. 104, read from the scan

Dett also wrote out his own version of it, trying, he said, "to transcribe the effect of the thousand voices of the school", in parts "so very simple and natural that no group of singers should be daunted by them".

source.en: R. Nathaniel Dett, ed., Religious Folk-Songs of the Negro as Sung at Hampton Institute (1927), p. 106, footnote, read from the scan
